recipes.name: G's Tres Leches Cake
ingredients_raw: 0.75 cup unsalted butter at room temperature
1.5 cups whole milk at room temperature

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 9x13-inch baking pan.

Cream 1 1/2 cup sugar and unsalted butter in a large bowl until mixture is fluffy and pale yellow, 3 to 5 minutes. Mix 6 egg yolks into the butter mixture, stirring in each one before adding the next. Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl; gradually stir the flour mixture into the egg yolk mixture, alternating with 1 1/2 cup milk, to make a smooth batter. Stir in almond extract.

Beat 6 egg whites with cream of tartar in a bowl with an electric mixer until frothy; gradually beat in 2 tablespoons sugar until the egg whites form stiff peaks. Gently fold the egg white mixture into the batter, retaining as much volume as possible. Pour the cake batter into prepared baking pan.
Bake in preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the middle of the cake comes out clean, 35 to 45 minutes. Cool cake completely in pan on a rack.
Whisk sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, and 2 tablespoons whole milk in a bowl. Use a large fork or skewer to poke holes all over the cake; pour the three-milk mixture over the cake.

Beat cream with 1/4 cup sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract until the whipped cream holds stiff peaks. Top the cake with whipped cream; refrigerate until cold, at least 1 hour. Refrigerate leftovers. Cake is better a day or two after making.

raw_recipe.headline: G's Tres Leches Cake
raw_recipe.description: A dense yet light tres leches (three milks) cake is topped with sweetened whipped cream. Serve this ultra-moist dessert well chilled; in fact, it's better after a day or so in the refrigerator.

review.reviewBody: I have heard of tres leche cakes for a long time..but never tried one..till now. I am an instant fan..this cake is the best thing I have put in my mouth in a long time. I am picky when it comes to cakes and this one is worth the time and the wait for the 2 days to enjoy it. The only changes I made was to use a 12 oz can of cocont milk instead of the evaporated milk, poured the milk sauce on when warm, and put on the whip cream after it was refrigerated for 2 days. and topped it with toasted coconut. This cake reminded me of a coconut cream pie souffle'

This tres leches cake came out perfect! I used 3 8” round pans and layered them with sliced mixed berries and whip cream in between each layer. It was my Mother’s Day treat to myself. I will definitely make this again,

Terrific recipe! I didn't have any canned evaporated milk or sweetened condensed milk, so I made my own by simmering down 6 c. organic whole milk mixed with 3/4 c. sucanat until the volume was reduced by about half. Then I stirred in 4 T of butter, 1 t. of vanilla extract and about 3/4 c. heavy cream before pouring it over the cake. Yum! This recipe also works well with sweetened condensed coconut milk.

I’ve been wanting to try a tres leches cake for a while now. This recipe had a solid 5-stars (as opposed to other recipes that had 4.5) so I decided to give it a try. I didn’t read the recipe ahead of time to see that half the ingredients needed to be room temperature, so everything I used was cold (right out of the fridge), which didn’t seem to make a difference – it turned out great! I used salted butter, which I microwaved for 15-seconds to make it “room temperature-ish”, so I omitted the extra salt. I followed all the other instructions. Also changed the almond extract to vanilla. I baked this in an 11x15 glass pan (instead of a metal one) so that I could leave the cake in the pan to absorb the milk mixture. Baked at 325 in convection oven for 45-minutes. Didn’t have whole milk so used 1-tbsp 2% and 1-tbsp of 18% cream. Made on Saturday night for Sunday supper so it was in the fridge for 24-hours before serving. Frosted with whipped cream right before serving. This cake was very dense but not soggy, and was very easy on the palette. It was a good dessert choice for after a very flavour-intense meal. You could also jazz this up a million different ways.

My god woman. First things first.. That's the best sponge cake recipe I've ever made. It was flawless! I can see this as is being so lovely on a hot day straight out of the fridge. I'm in IL in the fall however so I jazzed it up!! In the batter I halved the almond extract and added a full tsp of vanilla. I grated some fresh nutmeg (probably about 1/2tsp) and added some cinnamon (probably about 1/4tsp) and a shot of Rumchata. I also added another shot of Rumchata to the whipped cream and probably only used about half the sugar figuring the liquor likely adds some sweet too. And dusted the top w another bit of fresh nutmeg and cinnamon. Made it for a coworkers birthday who loves tres leches. He was SO happy! Resounding success. Thank you so much for sharing. This cake has so many possibilities. I'm going to have to make it again and again to satisfy my curiosity. Is anyone is looking for a good gift, I'm going to need a gym membership! Lol. Happy baking y'all!

I've made this recipe 4 times, all yielding many compliments (even though I overbaked the cake once) and without an electric mixer. If you're going to hand-whisk, I recommend halving the recipe as it's much easier to get the eggs and whipped cream to the right consistency. Using thickened cream instead of whipping cream also helps. I also tend to halve the sugar and butter content, which makes it taste lighter.

This is a great recipe. It may seem like a lot of liquid, but it gets absorbed into the cake very quickly. We didn't wait for the cake to cool before we poured the milk mixture on top, and it turned out beautifully. I was a little concerned because the cake rose up really high while it was cooking, but once I removed it from the oven and poked the holes into it, it fell enough so that the topping could be added. The cake turned out very moist and flavorful, but not as wet as other tres leches cakes I've had. The texture was wonderful. 

You can top it with toasted sliced almonds and fresh strawberries to make it extra special. It's the perfect dessert for summer and definitely better served the next day. My husband also tried it topped with coconut and with sliced bananas, and that was good too. You can really customize it to your own tastes. I like that you can bake it in a standard 13x9 inch pan. Other recipes I looked at required pan sizes that we don't have. Will definitely make this one again. Might try substituting vanilla extract for the almond next time, although the almond pairs great with fresh strawberries.

I fell in love with this recipe. I made it for my neighbor's birthday. 
I did tweak it a little. I used vanilla extract instead of almond extract. I just don't care for it. For the tres leches I used 1/3 of a cup of heavy cream instead of the whole milk. I'm lactose intolerant so tasting it was a bit of a sacrifice but worth it. I will be making this again but adding some strawberries. It was the best tres leches cake I've ever had.

Very good recipe. I made it exactly as written. Next time, I would omit the almond flavoring or reduce it to maybe a quarter teaspoon, it's just not to my taste (to much like Christmas cut out cookies). I would also cut back the sugar a little, maybe by 1/4 cup. don't worry about the liquid being too much it Will all be absorbed by the cake, in fact, it's probably more absorbed then some other tres leches cakes that I've had. the cake will be high and fluffy out of the oven, I ended up baking mine for 37 minutes the top was golden and a few cracks just starting in the middle. The cake will shrink and flatten out (becoming denser) as it cools, I ran a knife around the edges to loosen right away. Letting the cake cool will allow it to continue cooking in case the middle has any slightly gooey parts. All in all it got a thumbs up and with the changes should be a 5 star for me.

This cake was amazing! Made it just like the recipe said and it turned out great. A lot of reviews suggested letting it sit for a day before eating it, to let the cake soak up the milk. So, I impatiently let it sit in the fridge overnight. It was worth the wait! Everyone at the family party loved it.

The BEST tres leches I’ve ever made. Hands down. I made exactly as written, though I did not have whole milk so I opted for half and half, and I added toasted coconut to the top (personal preference). Out of this world good! Thank you for the recipe!

This is the third tres leches cake recipe I have tried from Allrecipes. I followed the recipe exactly (except using vanilla instead of almond extract). Hands down it is the worst of the 3. And, it was the most labor intensive. Definitely not "wet" enough. There should be some milk oozing out the bottom when you plate tres leches and there was not. This cake was just dense and chewy. The flavor was dull too.
I tweeted the recipe it a little . I added 1 teaspoon of cinnamon and no cream if tarter! And the result was delicious!!!

One word: OMG.

One of the more complicated variations out there (room temp, etc) BUT WORTH IT!

My son & I made it and we made a mess....but we had a great time doing it. Worth it! It was AMAZING!
delicious .. not a light cake, very moist and flavourful.. great served with a fruit sauce on top of th whipped cream. And definitely better after a couple of days.

I used a cake mix for this and it was too light, so made the cake a little too damp in the bottom for me. I made it for a group meeting and they loved it. Next time I will use the recommended recipe for the cake or use a pound cake. I will definitely do it again soon.
So good! It was large enough we couldn’t eat it all. I froze 4portion slices to eat later.

This cake gets five stars from me!! It’s probably been 10 years since I made a tres leches cake, so when my son requested one for his birthday, I scoured the internet & this was one of the few that had consistent five star ratings. And deservedly so! I followed the recipe exactly as written, only subbing extra vanilla for the almond extract, just because of personal taste. It did take the full 45 minutes to bake in my oven and I worried the edges might be dry, but no. I only let it cool slightly before pouring the milk mixture over the cake. It really absorbed all the liquid, no problem. I made it the day before so it had a chance to set up. I did add a 1/4 tsp of cinnamon to the whipped topping and then sprinkled the iced cake with cinnamon sugar. Everyone raves, especially my son. I’ll definitely be making this again!
It was so heavy and thick to eat. A stodgy consistency. Not a fan for the work it entailed.
It was wonderful! I only had salted butter, so I used that and then I didn't add the 1/2 tsp salt to the recipe. It turned out great!
